featured_reviews.name: Afzal Mohhamad
featured_reviews.review_text:
Pros: Nearest to marine lines station.That's it.

Cons: On 4th floor

Rooms size of matchboxes with costs of 3bhk.

They don't allow outside food inside the hostel, umm sorry I didn't know this was a movie theater that you are not allowing outside food.

1 unit electricity at 18Rs. Please note the reading or click a pic of the meter otherwise god help you.

Water is chargeable. Yes drinking water in a hostel is not free because it is a luxury.

Food per plate is 150rs. Guess I'll sleep empty stomach for half the month with these rates.

Staff. So professional and friendly. NOT.

FULL DISCLOSURE - I paid 15k for a 4 sharing matchbox. No meals included. No water taken by me because it is dispicable to be charged for it by the hostel. Electricity charge was 3k per person so 12k for 1 month for a room. If confused ask your papa what is the home's electrical bill for a month. You'll be surprised. That's it. featured_reviews.name: rohan vaswani
featured_reviews.review_text:
My Experience with Piramal Group – Repeated Defaults on Written Commitments

I am sharing this purely as my personal experience and opinion, based on direct interactions with Piramal Group’s senior representatives.

I was given multiple explicit assurances, including a specific written commitment that a credit note would be issued by 8 February. That promise has now been missed, repeatedly, without explanation, ownership, or even basic communication—despite escalations to senior management.

When an organisation of this scale fails to honour simple, routine financial commitments after multiple follow-ups, it raises serious concerns about internal accountability, governance, and execution discipline. What is most worrying is not the delay itself, but the complete absence of transparency or ownership.

As a customer, this experience has significantly eroded my confidence. Repeated missed timelines and silence create the unfortunate perception that commitments are made casually and honoured selectively.

I would strongly advise prospective customers to document everything in writing, be cautious with assurances, and factor in delays—even when commitments are made at senior levels.

This review reflects my experience alone, but it has been deeply disappointing.

featured_reviews.name: Rajkunwar Pawar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Extremely Disappointed with the After-Sales Experience

I would strongly advise against booking a property here. The after-sales service has been extremely poor, and the customer relationship management is frustrating to deal with. The CRM team seems to be trained only to follow up for payments and installations — any genuine customer concerns are consistently ignored.

We received an official invite claiming the amenities were completed and ready for viewing. We travelled from another city just for this, only to find that barely 10% of the amenities were ready — just two indoor rooms (Pilates & Cycling). This was highly misleading.

Despite making multiple visits — including two personal trips I made flying in from London — we have still not been shown the floor view of the completed building (South), even though that is a basic request. Our unit is in a different tower, but our only request was to see the floor view of a completed tower. Every time, we’ve been met with excuses like “we don’t have the keys” — even though possession hasn’t started yet.

The customer service is apathetic at best. Calls go unanswered, and emails regarding even simple customer requirements are ignored.

If this is the service before possession, it raises serious concerns about what can be expected after moving in.

featured_reviews.name: Faiz F
featured_reviews.review_text:
South Mumbai's Landmark
​Located in the historic and well-connected Byculla (Mahalaxmi) neighborhood of South Mumbai,

Planet Godrej stands as a monumental and striking example of modern architecture. Designed by Singapore-based DP Architects, this residential skyscraper complex, completed in 2009, has cemented its place as a key landmark and a symbol of luxury living in the city.

​Architectural and Landmark Status

The project is comprised of five towers, soaring 51 floors high. A notable design feature is that the towers occupy only about 5% of the total 9-acre plot, leaving a vast, landscaped open space for residents. This deliberate use of space, combined with its impressive height, has earned it several awards and the status of a landmark. From its upper floors, residents are treated to breathtaking, 360-degree panoramic views of the Arabian Sea, the iconic Haji Ali Mosque, and the Mahalaxmi Racecourse.

​Luxurious Amenities and Lifestyle

Planet Godrej is celebrated for its extensive and luxurious amenities, which are central to the premium lifestyle it offers. The complex includes a large, well-maintained swimming pool, a children's play area, and a jogging and strolling track. For sports and recreation, there are tennis courts, a squash court, a basketball court, and a modern, spacious gymnasium. Other facilities include a large clubhouse, landscaped gardens, and ample parking space. Residents also benefit from essential services such as power backup and an ATM within the premises.

​Premium Security

Security is a top priority at Planet Godrej, with multiple layers of protection to ensure a safe living environment. The complex is equipped with a modern security system, including CCTV cameras and a fire alarm system. Security guards are stationed at the main entrance and throughout the premises, regulating access for residents and visitors.

​Connectivity and Community

Its central location in Byculla offers excellent connectivity to various parts of the city via major roads and railway stations. While some residents have noted occasional noise pollution from the nearby railway tracks, the convenience of being close to schools, hospitals, and major business hubs is a significant advantage. The community is generally described as educated and decent, with a friendly atmosphere that contributes to a comfortable lifestyle.
